figures.label: FIGURE 4-3
figures.title: FIGURE 4-3 Using touch conveys a sense of caring and compassion.
figures.crossrefs: Touch is a powerful tool; therefore, keep in mind that it should be used consciously and sparingly (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-4
figures.title: FIGURE 4-4 Watch your body language, because patients may misinterpret your gestures, movements, and stance.
figures.crossrefs: Nonverbal communication is extremely important in dealing with patients (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-5
figures.title: FIGURE 4-5 You need a great deal of compassion and patience when caring for older patients. Never assume that a patient is senile or confused.
figures.crossrefs: In general, older people think clearly, can give you a clear medical history, and are able to answer your questions appropriately (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-6
figures.title: FIGURE 4-6 Maintain eye contact with a child to let the child know that you are there to help and that you can be trusted.
figures.crossrefs: Maintain eye contact with a child, as you would with an adult, to let the child know that you are there to help and that you can be trusted (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-15
figures.title: FIGURE 4-15 Some ambulances have more than one mobile radio to allow communications with hospitals, mutual aid jurisdictions, and other agencies.
figures.crossrefs: An ambulance will often have more than one mobile radio, each on a different frequency (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-16
figures.title: FIGURE 4-16 A portable radio is essential if you need to communicate with the dispatcher or medical control when you are away from the ambulance.
figures.crossrefs: They are also helpful when you are away from the ambulance and need to communicate with dispatch, another unit, or medical control (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-17
figures.title: FIGURE 4-17 A message is sent from the control center to the transmitter by a landline. The radio carrier wave is picked up by the repeater for rebroadcast to outlying units. Return radio traffic is picked up by the repeater and rebroadcast to the control center.
figures.crossrefs: The signal is then rebroadcast with all the power of the base station (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-18
figures.title: FIGURE 4-18 A mobile data terminal.
figures.crossrefs: Another type of communication system is a  mobile data terminal (MDT) (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-19
figures.title: FIGURE 4-19 You will be assigned to a call by the dispatcher.
figures.crossrefs: The dispatcher’s next step is to alert the appropriate EMS response unit or units (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-20
figures.title: FIGURE 4-20 The patient report should be given in an objective, accurate, and professional manner.
figures.crossrefs: The purpose of these calls is to notify the receiving facility of the patient’s chief complaint and condition (   ).

figures.label: FIGURE 4-21
figures.title: FIGURE 4-21 Medical control must be readily available on the radio or telephone at the hospital.
figures.crossrefs: To maintain this link 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, medical control must be readily available on the radio at the hospital or on a mobile or portable unit when you call (   ).
